paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. Two kings in a row on Judah's throne, and both of them walk in the ways of the house of Ahab. Jehoram "married a daughter of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the LORD," and his son Ahaziah did evil too, "for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab" (2 Kings 8:18, 27). The people closest to us shape the road we walk, and the Bible isn't shy about saying so.

Now look at what the passage says right in the middle of all that. "Yet for the sake of His servant David, the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah, since He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever" (2 Kings 8:19). Judah did not hold on because its kings were good. Judah held on because God keeps His promises. I've been in the back of a drawer, friend, and I can tell you it's a great comfort that God's faithfulness doesn't depend on how well anybody else is doing.

So what do you do with that today? Pay attention to whose ways you're walking in, and pick your company on purpose. Then lean your whole weight on the God who keeps His word, because He is the One who never runs out. This story isn't over, either, so keep your oven warm.
